title: Tidewater Pharma — inference requirements & POC scratchpad
content:
Meeting: Tidewater Pharma — 2026-03-08 11:00 PT (kickoff call)
Attendees: Priya (Redwood), Marcus (Redwood SE), Janelle (Redwood PM), Amir (Tidewater infra), Lina (Tidewater product), Dr. Gomez (Tidewater compliance)

Quick background
- Tidewater: mid-size pharma, manufacturing + clinical trials data. Very sensitive PII/PHI and product IP.
- Goal: add LLM-assisted SOP drafting + internal QA triage + search over trial protocols. Not public-facing.
- Preference for private deployment (VPC / on-prem) given regulatory concerns (GxP + EU data residency for some sites).

Primary requirements (first pass)
- Data residency: EU-hosted private control plane + data-at-rest in their GCP project (customer KMS).
- Audit logs: full request/response logging retained 2 years, exportable to Splunk.
- Encryption: HSM-backed keys for model weights not required yet, but KMS for tokenization artifacts required.
- SLA: 99.9% monthly uptime for core inference endpoints used by clinical ops.
- Throughput & latency: baseline 30–50 inference requests/sec for bulk triage; 200 req/s burst for nightly ingest jobs. Target p99 latency < 800ms for 512-token average requests.
- Cost sensitivity: procurement will push back on ongoing token spend; will test batching + caching to reduce unit cost.
- Model fidelity: must validate hallucination risk for SOP rewriting. Need eval harness using Tidewater prompts (privacy preserved).
- Embeddings: semantic search across protocols; embeddings store must be inside customer VPC or self-hosted vector DB.

Tech notes / ideas captured during call
- Private deployment model: Redwood Private (VPC) + optional on-prem connector for lab floor machines. Use dedicated capacity reservation for peak batch windows.
- Suggest quantized + 8-bit variants for cheaper throughput for non-critical batch re-runs; keep a higher-precision variant for SOP editing flows.
- Use prefix caching for frequent prompts (template-based SOP edits) — big win for cost.
- For embeddings, recommend sidecar vector DB (Pinecone/RedisTorch) inside customer's VPC. We can provide sample infra terraform.
- Compliance: generate a minimal audit template for Dr. Gomez to sign off: what is logged, who can view logs, retention and export process.

Gotchas / risks flagged
- Data flow: Tidewater ops unclear where clinical trial metadata currently stored; we must avoid pulling PHI into any hosted service until contracts signed.
- Legal: procurement insists on DPA and SOC2 plus evidence of GxP controls; timeline for legal review unknown — this may block POC.
- Throughput tests: Tidewater expects our numbers to match their on-prem hardware; we need a baseline benchmark on similar GPU class (A10G/RTX6000?) to set expectations.
- Embedding drift: search relevance will depend heavily on document normalization; they have scanned PDFs with OCR issues — preprocessing step required.

POC scope suggestion (lean)
- Phase 0 (safe): architecture review + security checklist signed by Tidewater security. Standup a demo VPC with sample de-identified dataset.
- Phase 1 (POC): 4-week POC: host Redwood Private in customer VPC, integrate with customer KMS, run two workloads: (1) interactive SOP rewrite flow with 95% fidelity target on evaluation set, (2) nightly batch embeddings + vector search with throughput test to 50 req/s sustained.
- Success criteria: 1) p99 latency < 1s for interactive flow on 512 tokens; 2) embedding similarity retrieval recall@10 > 0.85 on curated QA set; 3) logging and export validated by Tidewater security.

Action items (assignees & rough ETA)
- Priya: draft security checklist + sample DPA clauses for Tidewater legal (ETA: 2026-03-15)
- Marcus: run bench on A10G (local infra) and produce cost projection for 30/200 req/s patterns (ETA: 2026-03-11)
- Janelle: prepare POC SOW template + budget estimate (ETA: 2026-03-16)
- Amir (customer): confirm where clinical metadata lives and whether de-id pipeline exists (ETA: 2026-03-12)
- Lina (customer): assemble 50 de-identified SOPs and 200 sample queries for eval (ETA: 2026-03-18)
- Dr. Gomez: provide compliance checklist and highlight any GxP gaps we should be aware of (ETA: 2026-03-20)

Open questions / follow-ups
- Does Tidewater require on-prem model weights (air-gapped) for production? If yes, provisioning timeline changes.
- Confirm exact GPU families they can accept in their data centers / cloud (A10G vs A100).
- How strict is the retention policy — can we propose 90-day logs for initial POC and 2-year for production?
- Who is the procurement lead and what is the contracting timeline?

Notes to self (shorthand)
- Emphasize Redwood Optimize features (batching suggestions + quantization paths) in SOW — hits cost problem directly.
- Prep a short slide: "P0 compliance controls" for Dr. Gomez (one-pager) + mapping to Redwood controls.
- Put together a sanitized eval harness and share with Tidewater for independent validation.

Raw call transcript highlights (fragmented)
- Dr. Gomez: "We cannot have patient identifiers leave our GCP project until contracts are in place."
- Amir: "We have scheduled jobs that will pump 100k docs overnight, that's where cost spikes happen."
- Lina: "If the editor experience gets close, we'll pilot with 20 power users."

Next meeting: 2026-03-17 09:30 PT — technical deep-dive (Marcus + Amir + infra folks).

End of jot — keep in users (private) until we have legal OK to move to shared drive.
